clue.text: Fellow shot for harbouring pacifist

indicators.note: to harbour is to shelter, so the shot holds the pacifist within it

parts.note: a shot is an injection, a jab
CO stands for conscientious objector, a pacifist who refuses military service

explanation.surface: A man is shot dead for sheltering a peace campaigner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellow' reads as a member of a group, but it simply defines a man by his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow is a man, and the clue treats any male first name as an example of one.

clue.text: Judge June's marmalade fantastic, as WI are supposed to do?

definitions.text: as WI are supposed to do?

indicators.note: fantastic means wildly fanciful, so the letters are rearranged freely

parts.note: the possessive S counts here as a letter of the fodder

explanation.surface: A judge pronounces June's marmalade superb, as the Women's Institute should.
explanation.walkthrough: The WI is the Women's Institute, a British rural women's club stereotyped for making jam and singing the hymn Jerusalem at meetings.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is the stock description of what the Women's Institute does: making preserves and singing Blake's hymn.

clue.text: Coax journo to keep odd pieces in French dialect

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters, first, third and fifth, are kept

explanation.surface: Persuade a reporter to keep stray fragments of a French dialect.
explanation.definitionFit: Cajun is the French dialect of Louisiana descendants of Acadian settlers.

clue.text: Food that's Mexican — or Polish, on reflection — contains it

indicators.note: the reversed pair holds the last word inside it
a mirror reflection runs backwards, so both words are read right to left

parts.note: to polish is to rub
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Mexican dish, or something Polish if you think about it, includes this.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital pretends to be the nationality; it is the verb rub. 'on reflection' turns OR and RUB into BURRO, which holds IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A burrito is a tortilla wrapped round a filling, a Mexican food.

clue.text: Fitting time to smother cry in Spanish opera

indicators.note: smothering covers something completely, so the fitting piece wraps round the Spanish cry

parts.note: a rig is fitting or equipment, as on a ship
taken as written
ole is the Spanish shout of approval at a bullfight

explanation.surface: A clever stage moment silences a shout during a Spanish opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spanish opera' wants to run together, but Spanish belongs to the cry; the opera itself is Verdi's, set in Mantua.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Verdi's opera about the hunchbacked court jester, so the work is an example of opera.

clue.text: Do cornerpiece and also flier

definitions.meaning: to do someone is to swindle or cheat them
the chess piece that starts on a corner square
a black crow-like bird that nests in colonies

explanation.definitionFit: Rook means to swindle, names the chess castle that starts in a corner, and is a bird of the crow family.

clue.text: Make a public statement: say "I'm walking backwards for Christmas"

definitions.meaning: to state one's position openly and formally
this comic song was a 1956 hit single by the Goons, Spike Milligan's comedy team

explanation.walkthrough: The Goons were the British radio comedy team of Milligan, Sellers and Secombe; their song is a record by Goons.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on record is to state something publicly; read as three words it describes a disc by the Goons.

clue.text: Various dailies got in touch

indicators.note: various means assorted, so the letters are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Several newspapers made contact.
explanation.definitionFit: To liaise is to communicate and cooperate, so liaised means made contact.

clue.text: Called out the number of weeds dealt with?

parts.note: a tally is a running count or number
weeds are dealt with when hoed out

explanation.surface: A gardener announced how many weeds had been tackled.
explanation.walkthrough: Tally-ho is the huntsman's cry on sighting the fox, so to tally-ho is to call out.
explanation.definitionFit: To tally-ho is to give the huntsman's shout, so tally-hoed means called out.

clue.text: The conifers' weight eclipsed by potato: brilliant!

parts.note: the possessive turned round reads of the firs

indicators.note: an eclipsed body is hidden behind another, so the weight sits inside the potato

parts.note: tater is a dialect word for potato

explanation.surface: A potato outweighing the pine trees: brilliant!
explanation.walkthrough: 'eclipsed by' puts W inside TATER to make TWATER, following the possessive rewritten as a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Of the first water describes a diamond of the finest clarity, so by extension anything brilliant or excellent.

clue.text: Official in House has mother and girl first in reckoning, party second

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother
Jo is a girl's name

indicators.note: the opening letter of the following word is all that is used

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A House official's paperwork lists mother, then a girl, with a party coming second.
explanation.definitionFit: A major-domo is the chief steward running a great household, an official of the house.

clue.text: Vatican delegate recalling brave Mother Teresa? Not her

indicators.note: recalling calls back, so the combined letters are read in reverse order
not her says the letters of her are removed from the brave word

parts.note: heroic means brave
the word her as written is the part dropped
Mother Teresa was a famous Roman Catholic nun

explanation.surface: A papal envoy remembers the courageous Mother Teresa, though she is not the one meant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not her' seems to deny that Mother Teresa is the envoy, but it cuts three letters from the brave word, leaving OIC; 'recalling' then turns the whole run round.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuncio is a papal ambassador, the Holy See's diplomatic representative to a country.

clue.text: Petrol's spilled round far end of grimy porch

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the extra letter
spilt liquid scatters, so the letters of the fuel word are thrown into a new order

parts.note: the possessive is read as the word plus an S, giving seven letters to shuffle

indicators.note: the far end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Fuel spilt around a filthy porch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilled' makes PROSTLE from PETROLS, and 'round' puts it round Y, the last letter of 'grimy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prostyle is an architectural term for a portico with a row of columns standing in front, a kind of porch.

clue.text: Express, perhaps, in row grand, empty threat

parts.note: the Daily Express is an example of a newspaper

indicators.note: the grand sits inside the row

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
G is slang for a grand, a thousand pounds

explanation.surface: A newspaper row over a big sum turns out to be all bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Express' looks like the verb to state; it is the British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper tiger looks threatening but is powerless, so it is an empty threat.

clue.text: Brazilian very much committed at first to capture New Orleans girl

indicators.note: capturing takes something prisoner inside, so the Brazilian holds the letter

parts.note: Joao is a very common Brazilian man's name
far means very much, as in far better

indicators.note: only the first letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: A dedicated Brazilian sets out to take over New Orleans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New Orleans' is the trap: only 'New' is wordplay, and 'Orleans girl' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan of Arc, the Maid of Orleans, raised the siege of that French city in 1429.

clue.text: Place around pole bow that's intact, somehow, externally

indicators.note: the shuffled letters lie outside the bow
somehow says the letters arrive in some unstated order, an anagram

parts.note: a bow is an arc, a curve

explanation.surface: A bow survives undamaged on an expedition near the pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bow' looks like the archer's weapon or a ship's front; here it is any curve. 'somehow' makes ANTTIC from the fodder, which 'externally' wraps round the curve.
explanation.definitionFit: The Antarctic is the region surrounding the South Pole.

clue.text: Going west, pass round stolen Indian attire

indicators.note: the turned pass goes round the stolen goods
in an across entry west is leftwards, so the pass is written backwards

parts.note: an ID card is a pass that admits you
hot is slang for stolen

explanation.surface: Heading west, a stolen Indian garment is handed round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going west' turns the pass into DI before 'round' sets it about the stolen goods; a dhoti is draped round the waist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the loincloth worn by many Hindu men, a traditional Indian garment.

clue.text: Openings in real estate that country houses seem to throw up

indicators.note: each word's opening, its first letter, is taken in turn

explanation.surface: Seen from outside, the country houses on this real estate look almost sick-making.
explanation.definitionFit: To retch is to heave as if vomiting, which is what throwing up involves.

clue.text: Push and pull!

parts.note: read two ways: the push as being sacked, and an order to haul a rope

explanation.definitionFit: Getting the heave-ho is being dismissed, and the cry itself urges sailors to haul together.

clue.text: As tragedian you read out letters on grave and murderous date

indicators.note: two letters said aloud make the sound of the word you

parts.note: the word you is the sound the first two letters make
RIP, rest in peace, is carved on gravestones
Caesar was murdered on the Ides of March

explanation.surface: To play tragedy you recite lines over a grave on a fatal day.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening two letters are pronounced 'you' in this name, so 'you read out' gives letters, not a word.
explanation.definitionFit: Euripides was one of the three great Athenian tragic playwrights, author of Medea.

clue.text: After exercising I've turned quiet and irritable

indicators.note: after says the following pieces come behind the exercise

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

indicators.note: turned round means the letters are written in reverse

parts.note: the contraction's letters, without the apostrophe
sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: After a workout I've become withdrawn and short-tempered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' makes EVI from IVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Peevish means fretful and easily annoyed, a synonym of irritable.

clue.text: Catching right coach becomes hard for those waiting

indicators.note: catching means holding, so the setting word holds the next two pieces

parts.note: concrete or jelly sets when it becomes hard
a van is an old word for a coach or carriage

explanation.surface: Getting the right coach becomes a struggle for people in the queue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'those waiting' looks like a queue but means people who wait on others at table.
explanation.definitionFit: Servants wait on their employers, so those who wait at table are servants.

clue.text: Rise and fall of Lincoln, say, and return of Washington

parts.note: 'of Lincoln' is read as the possessive of a see, the diocese Lincoln is an example of

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: WA is the postal abbreviation of Washington state

explanation.surface: Lincoln's rise and fall and Washington's comeback, two US presidents compared.
explanation.walkthrough: Lincoln and Washington look like presidents; Lincoln is the English cathedral city, and 'of' makes its see possessive, so an extra S.
explanation.definitionFit: A seesaw goes up and down repeatedly, a movement of rising and falling.

clue.text: Fabulous hunted creature's singular snout

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
snout and nark are both slang for a police informer

explanation.surface: A mythical quarry has a peculiar nose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snout' looks like a nose; it is slang for an informer.
explanation.definitionFit: The snark is the imaginary beast pursued in Lewis Carroll's nonsense poem The Hunting of the Snark.

clue.text: Dashed fine sergeant is missing!

parts.note: F is the pencil abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: the letters of is go missing from the sergeant

parts.note: Lewis was Inspector Morse's sergeant in the TV detective series

explanation.surface: Blast, the good sergeant has disappeared!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dashed' reads as a mild oath; it means rushed. Inspector Morse was a British TV detective drama set in Oxford.
explanation.definitionFit: Dashed means rushed, and flew is used for moving very fast.

clue.text: Turned on gas light

parts.note: a lamp turned on is lit
He is the chemical symbol of helium, a gas

explanation.surface: Someone switched on the gas lamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas light' reads as one thing; 'light' alone is the definition, in its sense of nimble.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means supple and agile, light on one's feet.

clue.text: Visiting Gretna, villagers recalled tour for pleasure

indicators.note: recalling calls back, so the run is read backwards
a visitor is inside a place for a while, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: Villagers of Gretna remember a pleasure trip they took.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visiting' takes TNAVILLAG from inside 'Gretna, villagers', and 'recalled' turns it round. Gretna Green is the Scottish village famous for runaway weddings.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to roam about looking for fun, travelling round for pleasure.

clue.text: Miniature-scale beer mug can appear in minutes, I boasted

indicators.note: the mugging word turns up inside the others

parts.note: crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast
to mug someone is to rob them

explanation.surface: Boasting that a tankard of small-batch beer can be downed in minutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mug' looks like the beer glass but is the verb; crowed has an old past tense alongside the modern one.
explanation.definitionFit: A microbrew is beer made in small quantities by a tiny brewery.

clue.text: No problem for lift-seeker: he'll give one

indicators.note: no problem means the problem word is taken away

parts.note: a hitchhiker thumbs lifts from passing drivers
a hitch is a problem or snag

explanation.surface: A hitchhiker's sunny reply: no problem, he'll offer one in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to a lift, and a hike is a lift in the sense of a raise, so a walker is one who gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: Hike also means to raise or lift, so a person who hikes gives a lift, a pun on hitching rides.
